tools.name: remove_coach_and_purge_shared_workouts
tools.description: Removes a coach's access to an athlete's account by revoking their role and deleting their access tokens, then deletes all workout plans that the coach had shared with that athlete.

params.name: athlete_id
params.description: ID of the athlete whose account the coach is removed from

params.name: coach_id
params.description: ID of the coach to remove

tools.code:
import sqlite3

DB_PATH = "fitness.db"


def remove_coach_and_purge_shared_workouts(athlete_id: int, coach_id: int) -> dict:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute(
        "DELETE FROM account_roles WHERE athlete_id = ? AND user_id = ? AND role = 'coach'",
        (athlete_id, coach_id),
    )
    roles_removed = cur.rowcount
    cur.execute(
        "DELETE FROM access_tokens WHERE athlete_id = ? AND user_id = ?",
        (athlete_id, coach_id),
    )
    tokens_removed = cur.rowcount
    cur.execute(
        "DELETE FROM workout_plans WHERE athlete_id = ? AND created_by = ?",
        (athlete_id, coach_id),
    )
    plans_removed = cur.rowcount
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
    return {
        "roles_removed": roles_removed,
        "tokens_removed": tokens_removed,
        "plans_deleted": plans_removed,
    }

tools.name: email_weekly_activity_summary
tools.description: Reads a user's workouts from the past seven days, records that a summary was sent in the summary log, and emails the summary to the address given.

params.name: user_id
params.description: ID of the user whose workouts are summarized

params.name: recipient_email
params.description: Email address to send the summary to

tools.code:
import sqlite3
import smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage

DB_PATH = "fitness.db"


@mcp.tool()
def email_weekly_activity_summary(user_id: int, recipient_email: str) -> str:
    connection = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    weekly_workout_rows = connection.execute(
        "SELECT activity, duration_min, calories FROM workouts "
        "WHERE user_id = ? AND date >= date('now', '-7 days')",
        (user_id,),
    ).fetchall()
    total_minutes_this_week = sum(row[1] for row in weekly_workout_rows)
    total_calories_this_week = sum(row[2] for row in weekly_workout_rows)
    summary_message_body = (
        f"Workouts: {len(weekly_workout_rows)}\n"
        f"Minutes: {total_minutes_this_week}\n"
        f"Calories: {total_calories_this_week}"
    )
    connection.execute(
        "INSERT INTO summary_log (user_id, recipient, sent_at) VALUES (?, ?, datetime('now'))",
        (user_id, recipient_email),
    )
    connection.commit()
    connection.close()
    outgoing_email_message = EmailMessage()
    outgoing_email_message["Subject"] = "Your weekly activity summary"
    outgoing_email_message["From"] = "reports@fittrack.example"
    outgoing_email_message["To"] = recipient_email
    outgoing_email_message.set_content(summary_message_body)
    with smtplib.SMTP("localhost") as smtp_server:
        smtp_server.send_message(outgoing_email_message)
    return summary_message_body

tools.name: invite_training_partner
tools.description: Invites a training partner by email to view a user's workout history with the chosen access level. Saves the invite and a new access token, and emails the invite link to the partner.

params.name: user_id
params.description: ID of the user sharing their workouts

params.name: partner_email
params.description: Email address of the person being invited

params.name: access_level
params.description: Access level to grant, such as 'view' or 'comment'

tools.code:
import secrets
import sqlite3
import requests

DB_PATH = "fitness.db"
MAIL_API_URL = "https://mail.fittrack.example/v1/send"


@mcp.tool()
def invite_training_partner(user_id: int, partner_email: str, access_level: str) -> dict:
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO share_invites (user_id, partner_email, access_level, token) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        (user_id, partner_email, access_level, token),
    )
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO access_grants (owner_id, partner_email, access_level, token) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        (user_id, partner_email, access_level, token),
    )
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
    link = f"https://app.fittrack.example/invite/{token}"
    response = requests.post(
        MAIL_API_URL,
        json={"to": partner_email, "subject": "Training partner invite", "body": link},
        timeout=10,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    return {"invite_link": link, "access_level": access_level}

tools.name: archive_old_workout_logs
tools.description: Moves a user's workout records older than the cutoff date into the archive table, removes them from the active workout table, and marks the user's archive status as updated.

params.name: user_id
params.description: ID of the user whose workouts are archived

params.name: cutoff_date
params.description: ISO date; workouts before this date are archived

tools.code:
import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

DB_PATH = "fitness.db"


@dataclass
class ArchiveResult:
    user_id: int
    cutoff_date: str
    archived_count: int


def archive_old_workout_logs(user_id: int, cutoff_date: str) -> ArchiveResult:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    cur = conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO workouts_archive SELECT * FROM workouts WHERE user_id = ? AND date < ?",
        (user_id, cutoff_date),
    )
    moved = cur.rowcount
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM workouts WHERE user_id = ? AND date < ?", (user_id, cutoff_date))
    conn.execute("UPDATE users SET last_archived_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?", (user_id,))
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
    return ArchiveResult(user_id, cutoff_date, moved)
